name: Galaxy Generation & Navigation
summary: Galaxy generation implementation is largely faithful to design specs with good coverage of core algorithms. Found 4 high-severity mismatches (Orion planet environment, growth multipliers, Artifacts RP bonus formula), 3 medium-severity issues (scanner range confusion, exploration docs inconsistencies), and several low-severity style issues. Pathfinding, fleet actions, and starmap rendering are well-implemented. Some design features like wormholes and space monsters are defined in state but not yet implemented in generation.

matches.description: Galaxy size configurations match exactly: Small=24 stars (500×400), Medium=48 stars (700×560), Large=70 stars (850×680), Huge=108 stars (1000×800)
MIN_STAR_DISTANCE=35 parsecs matches design §10.1 constant
CLUSTER_RADIUS=60 matches design §10.1 constant
NEBULA_MIN_RADIUS=60 and NEBULA_MAX_RADIUS=120 match design §10.1
CLUSTER_PLACEMENT_CHANCE=0.70 matches design §2.3 algorithm (70% chance near cluster)
NEBULA_RESOURCE_BONUS_CHANCE=0.40 matches design §5.3 (40% chance to upgrade)
Star color weights match design §2.4: yellow=25, green=15, red=25, blue=15, white=12, purple=8
Environment probability tables for all 6 star colors match design §4.3 exactly
Planet size distribution matches design §4.4: tiny=15, small=25, medium=30, large=20, huge=10
Base population by size matches design §4.4: tiny=20, small=40, medium=60, large=80, huge=100
Resource distribution tables by star color match design §5.2 exactly
Homeworld configuration matches design §8.3: Terran environment, Large or Huge size, Normal resources, 40 starting population, 30 starting factories
Region assignment algorithm matches design §3.3: omega_sector < 0.15, nebula → dark_sectors, > 0.75 → safe_zones, else wild_pellet_fields
Nebula generation requires minimum 2 stars and uses overlap prevention per design §7.2-7.3
Artifacts placement algorithm prefers middle-ring (30%-70%) stars as specified in design §6.2
Cluster identification algorithm matches design §3.2 (find nearby stars within cluster radius, require 2+ neighbors)
Star names pool includes canonical MOO1 names as listed in design §2.5
Gaussian distribution used for clustered star placement matches design §2.3 GenerateClusteredPosition
Isolated star fixing algorithm matches design §11.4: move stars closer to nearest neighbor when beyond max range
Placement failure handling with reduced minimum distance (×0.9) matches design §11.1
10 maximum retry limit for galaxy generation matches design §11.5
Dijkstra's algorithm correctly implements shortest path finding for fleet routing
Pathfinding respects maxRange parameter for fuel range limits
StarSystem type includes all required fields: starType, hasNebula, isOrion, hasGuardian, hasArtifacts, region
Planet type includes resourceLevel, researchMultiplier, isRich, isPoor, isGaia, hasArtifacts as specified
GalaxyRegion enum includes all 4 regions: safe_zones, wild_pellet_fields, dark_sectors, omega_sector
Star color palette matches the 6 star types: yellow, green, red, blue, white, purple

mismatches.actual_impl: Orion planet is set to environment: 'dead' with basePop: 150. Code comment references design/planets/generation-tables.md §10.2, but generation-algorithm.md §6.1 specifies 'gaia' with base_pop 100.
mismatches.recommendation: Reconcile design docs: either update generation-algorithm.md §6.1 to match planets/generation-tables.md, or update code to use 'gaia' environment. The code comment suggests generation-tables.md §10.2 is the authoritative source, but this should be verified and generation-algorithm.md updated for consistency.

mismatches.design_spec: §4.5: 'gaia: {"growth_mult": 2.0, "pop_mult": 1.0}' — Gaia planets should have 2× growth rate
mismatches.actual_impl: ENVIRONMENT_POP_MULT only stores population multipliers. Growth multipliers from design §4.5 (e.g., gaia: 2.0, tundra: 0.5) are not captured or applied anywhere in galaxy generation.
mismatches.recommendation: Add ENVIRONMENT_GROWTH_MULT constant mapping environment types to growth multipliers from design §4.5. Apply this when creating Planet objects, setting the growthRate field appropriately.

mismatches.design_spec: §Artifacts Worlds: 'Ongoing RP Multiplier (persistent): all RP generated there is multiplied by 1.25 (+25%)'
mismatches.actual_impl: Artifacts planets are assigned researchMultiplier: 2.0 (100% bonus), not 1.25 (25% bonus). This contradicts exploration.md but matches generation-algorithm.md §6.2 which specifies 2× research.
mismatches.recommendation: Reconcile design docs: exploration.md says 1.25×, generation-algorithm.md §6.2 says 2×. Update exploration.md to match generation-algorithm.md (2× appears to be the intended authoritative value matching MOO1 behavior).

mismatches.design_spec: §8.4 Table: 'MinHomeworldDistance = GalaxyDiagonal × 0.25' yields Small=160, Medium=224, Large=272, Huge=320
mismatches.actual_impl: GALAXY_CONFIGS uses minHomeworldDistance: 150/175/200/225 from §1.2 config block. Code comment at line 45-52 explains this discrepancy: the formula values are 'too strict for reliable homeworld placement' and the config values are 'tested and working'.
mismatches.recommendation: Design doc §8.4 should be updated to note that the formula is theoretical and the actual implementation uses the §1.2 config values for practical reasons, or the formula should be removed to avoid confusion.

mismatches.design_spec: §Scanner Range: 'Base range: 2 parsecs... Scanner range is improved by Computers field technologies (e.g., Deep Space Scanner: 4 parsecs, Subspace Scanner: 6 parsecs)'
mismatches.actual_impl: Empire.scannerTechLevel is defined as 'number' with comment '0 = basic, +1 per upgrade', but there's no constant defining the base scanner range (2 parsecs) or the formula for calculating actual scanner range from tech level.
mismatches.recommendation: Add scanner range constants to a config file or the state module. Define BASE_SCANNER_RANGE = 2 and a formula/table mapping scannerTechLevel to actual range. This is needed for fog of war and exploration mechanics.

mismatches.design_spec: §Warp Speed Table: 'Retro Engines=1, Nuclear=2, Sub-Light=2, Fusion=3, Impulse=3, Ion=4, Anti-Matter=5, Interphased=6, Hyperdrives=7, Hyper-X=8, Temporal=9'
mismatches.actual_impl: Pathfinding takes maxRange parameter but there's no warp speed integration. The pathfinding doesn't calculate travel time (distance ÷ warp speed = turns). Fleet movement system would need this.
mismatches.recommendation: The pathfinding module should either include travel time calculation or document that it's purely for range validation. Add a separate function or extend PathResult to include turnsToArrive based on warp speed.

mismatches.design_spec: §Nebulae: 'Ships reduced to Warp 1 speed' — movement through nebulae should be slowed
mismatches.actual_impl: Pathfinding uses straight Euclidean distance without accounting for nebula slow-down. Paths through nebulae should have weighted edges (higher effective distance) to model the Warp 1 restriction.
mismatches.recommendation: Modify pathfinding to accept nebula data and apply a movement penalty (effective distance multiplier) when path segments cross nebula regions. Alternatively, handle this in the fleet movement system when calculating ETA.

mismatches.design_spec: §2.5: Star names include 'Thuban' listed twice in the pool
mismatches.actual_impl: STAR_NAMES array does not include 'Thuban' duplicate from design — it appears the code correctly de-duplicated. The design doc has a typo listing 'Thuban' at both position 87 and position 107.
mismatches.recommendation: Remove duplicate 'Thuban' from design/galaxy/generation-algorithm.md §2.5 star_names JSON array.

mismatches.actual_impl: STARTING_RANGE = 45 is defined and used for homeworld neighbor counting, but the relationship '3 parsecs × 15 display scale' is not documented in code. The magic number 15 for display scale should be a named constant.
mismatches.recommendation: Add DISPLAY_SCALE = 15 constant and use it consistently. Document that galaxy coordinates are in 'display units' = parsecs × 15.

mismatches.design_spec: §Planet Environments Table: Shows 'Gaia' at top with 'Huge' base pop cap, but notes say 'Gaia environments are only created through Soil Enrichment II technology transformation'
mismatches.actual_impl: ENVIRONMENT_TABLES correctly set gaia: 0 for all star colors (can't spawn naturally), but the code also handles 'gas_giant' type which is not in the design environment tables.
mismatches.recommendation: Clarify whether gas_giant is a valid planet type. It's in the PlanetType enum and ENVIRONMENT_TABLES but design docs don't mention it. Either add to design or remove from code.

missing_from_code.feature: Space Monsters (Amoeba and Crystal): Random events after Turn 100 that attack planets. MonsterType is defined in state.ts but no generation or behavior code exists.
Random Events system: Events like Ancient Derelict, Fertile Planet, Comet, Plague, etc. are described but no event generation code exists in galaxy generator.
Wormholes: hasWormhole and wormholeTarget fields exist in StarSystem type but no wormhole generation code exists in galaxy.ts.
Artifacts first-scout tech bonus: 'First scout bonus: One random technology at current tier + 1-3' is not implemented — only the research multiplier is set during generation.
Star Gates: 'Intergalactic Star Gates (3000 BC each)' for instant travel between gated planets. No Star Gate building or routing support in pathfinding.
Reserve Fuel Tanks (+3 parsecs) and Extended Fuel Tanks (+6 parsecs) special equipment effects on ship range. Not integrated with pathfinding maxRange.
§8.5 ValidateHomeworldNeighbors quality check: Code counts neighbors but doesn't validate average quality score or emit warnings for low_quality_neighbors.
Guardian ship placement at Orion: hasGuardian flag is set on the system and planet, but no actual Guardian ship/fleet entity is created during generation.

not_in_design.feature: PlanetType includes 'gas_giant' which is not documented in any design spec for planet environments.
starClassForType() maps star colors to spectral classes (G, K, M, O, A, NS) — this astronomical classification detail isn't in design docs.
QuadTreeNode spatial index for fast star lookups — this optimization structure isn't described in design docs (but is a reasonable implementation detail).
calculatePlanetQuality() is exported for tests but the quality scoring algorithm, while matching design §8.5, is implementation detail not explicitly required to be public.
drawFleetInTransit() with progress-based positioning along route — fleet animation details not specified in design docs.
Fleet deployment mode UI state (OPEN_FLEET_DEPLOYMENT, UPDATE_DEPLOYMENT_SHIPS, etc.) — detailed UI workflow not specified in travel.md design.
